expected_during_serial_loss: cumulative blood loss increases by each applied loss increment
blood volume and preload decrease as net loss accumulates
expected_after_partial_replacement: preload, flow, MAP, and CVP improve relative to the immediately preceding depleted state
state remains below original euvolemic baseline because replacement has not caught up with loss
cumulative input ledger increases only by delivered replacement
expected_after_loss_resumes: preload, flow, MAP, and CVP deteriorate from the partially corrected state
drainage pressure becomes more negative again
expected_after_remaining_net_deficit_rep: patient-directed ECMO flow returns approximately to baseline
drainage pressure returns approximately to baseline
notes: Serial 5% loss increments are regression stimuli, not validated neonatal hemorrhage thresholds.
The contract tests cumulative authoritative volume-ledger state, not monitor-number patches.
Replacement that does not keep pace with ongoing loss may improve hemodynamics without resolving the net deficit.
